title: Scheme relative differentials agree with differentials on the small etale ringed topos
statement: Let $f:U\to V$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Regard $U,V$ as representable algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use their small etale ringed topoi and the canonical ringed morphism $(f_{\mathrm{et}},f^\sharp)$ [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Put $\mathcal A=f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{V,\mathrm{et}}$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}$. Define $\Omega^{\mathrm{et}}_{U/V}$ as the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $W\mapsto\Omega_{\mathcal B(W)/\mathcal A(W)}$, using ring differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and their functorial restriction maps; it has the derivation induced by the sectionwise universal derivations. Modules mean [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F=\Omega^1_{U/V}$ be the usual Zariski relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ be its associated etale module [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. There is a canonical $\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}$-linear isomorphism $F_{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega^{\mathrm{et}}_{U/V}$ identifying the associated universal derivation with the sectionwise-induced universal derivation. No finite-type, finite-presentation, flatness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04CS, lemma-match-modules-differentials, statement and derivation-normalized isomorphism; Tag 04CT, definition-sheaf-differentials, for representable spaces.

proof.text: For an etale object $h:W\to U$, apply [lem-sfb-etale-localization-relative-differentials] with $X_2=W$, $X_1=U$, and $S_2=S_1=V$. Write $q_h:h^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega^1_{W/V}$ for the canonical map. Define $d^a_W(s)=q_h^{-1}(d_{W/V}s)$ in $F_{\mathrm{et}}(W)=\Gamma(W,h^*F)$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. It is additive and satisfies Leibniz. For an arrow $g:W'\to W$ over $U$, the two maps from $g^*h^*F$ to $\Omega^1_{W'/V}$ obtained by composing the canonical differential maps agree: by the scheme differential universal property and module-pullback adjunction, both are determined by sending each pulled-back $da$ to $d((hg)^\sharp a)$. Thus the $q_h$ agree with the pullback composition comparisons. Since $g$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], the same localization theorem applies to it, and its formula gives $d^a_W(s)|_{W'}=d^a_{W'}(g^\sharp s)$. Hence $d^a:\mathcal B\to F_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an additive sheaf map satisfying Leibniz.

source.place: Tag 04CS, first proof paragraph, using More on Morphisms Tag 04BX and Morphisms Tag 01UV (lemma-functoriality-differentials).

proof.text: The map $d^a$ annihilates the image of $\mathcal A=f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{V,\mathrm{et}}$. Indeed, on an etale object $W\to U$ the localization and composition identifications of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] identify the restriction of this inverse image with that for $W\to V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-section-description], any section is, on an etale cover $W_i\to W$, represented by a regular function on some etale $V_i\to V$ and a map $W_i\to V_i$ over $V$. Apply the localization theorem to the square $X_2=X_1=W_i$, $S_2=V_i$, $S_1=V$, with source arrow the identity. It identifies $\Omega^1_{W_i/V}$ with $\Omega^1_{W_i/V_i}$ on universal differentials. The differential of the pulled-back function is zero, by the base-vanishing clause of the scheme universal derivation. Consequently $d^a$ kills the given section after this cover and therefore globally by the sheaf axiom. This proves that $d^a$ is an $\mathcal A$-derivation.

source.place: Tag 04CS, first proof paragraph, base-linearity of d^a; Tag 04BX and Etale Cohomology Tag 09XN, lemma-describe-pullback, for local inverse-image sections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel] to the sheaves $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. It identifies the module sheafification in the statement with the representing sheaf for $\mathcal A$-derivations, with the specified $d_{\mathrm{et}}$. Therefore $d^a$ gives a unique $\mathcal B$-linear map $c:\Omega^{\mathrm{et}}_{U/V}\to F_{\mathrm{et}}$ satisfying $c\,d_{\mathrm{et}}=d^a$.

source.place: Tag 04CS, first proof paragraph: the map c; Modules on Sites Tags 04BL, 04BN and 08TP.

proof.text: Let $G$ be any $\mathcal B$-module sheaf and $D:\mathcal B\to G$ an $\mathcal A$-derivation. Put $G_U(A)=G(A\hookrightarrow U)$ for Zariski opens $A$ of $U$; this is the module direct image of [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections]. The restriction $D_U:\mathcal O_U\to G_U$ is a usual $V$-derivation: the section induced by any regular function on an open of $V$ is in the image of $\mathcal A$, so $D_U$ kills it. By [lem-sfb-relative-differentials-sheaf-universal-property] it factors uniquely as $\psi d_{U/V}$ with $\psi:F\to G_U$ linear. Apply [lem-trf-etale-tensor-sections-adjunction-extension] to $\psi$. Since $F$ is quasi-coherent, its presheaf $P_F$ there is exactly the already-sheaf $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ of [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. We obtain a linear map $\beta_D:F_{\mathrm{et}}\to G$ whose restriction to every Zariski open is $\psi$, under the unit-compatible identification. In particular $(\beta_Dd^a)|_{U_{\mathrm{Zar}}}=D_U$.

source.place: Tag 04CS, second and third proof paragraphs: restrict to Zariski opens and extend by the ringed-site adjunction; Descent Tags 070S and 03FH.

proof.text: In fact $\beta_Dd^a=D$ on every etale object. The difference $E=\beta_Dd^a-D$ is a derivation and is zero on all Zariski opens of $U$ by Step 4. Cover an etale $W\to U$ by affine opens $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into affine opens $A_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $U$. The map $T\to A_0$ is etale by the open-immersion, composition and cancellation clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Naturality implies that $E_T:B\to G(T)$ vanishes on the image of $A$, since $E_{A_0}=0$. It is therefore an $A$-derivation. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $\Omega_{B/A}=0$. The ring universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] forces $E_T=0$. Hence $E_W=0$ by the sheaf axiom for the indicated open cover. No intersection of affine opens was assumed affine, and no quasi-coherence of $G$ was used.

source.place: Tag 04CS, final omitted verification, expanded by the affine derivation argument; Morphisms Tag 02GJ and Algebra Tag 00U1. This step is the elementary factorization of an A-derivation through Omega_{B/A}=0.

proof.text: If $\alpha:F_{\mathrm{et}}\to G$ also satisfies $\alpha d^a=D$, its restriction to the Zariski opens factors the same derivation $D_U$. The uniqueness in [lem-sfb-relative-differentials-sheaf-universal-property] gives $\alpha|_{U_{\mathrm{Zar}}}=\psi=\beta_D|_{U_{\mathrm{Zar}}}$. Now [lem-trf-etale-tensor-sections-open-determination], with $M=F$ and target $G$, gives $\alpha=\beta_D$. Thus $d^a$ has the full universal factorization property, with the specified sectionwise formulas.

source.place: Tag 04CS, final paragraph: uniqueness of the map out of the associated differential module, using Descent Tag 070S/03FH adjunction.

proof.text: Take $G=\Omega^{\mathrm{et}}_{U/V}$ and $D=d_{\mathrm{et}}$ in Steps 4--6, and write $b=\beta_D$. Then $b d^a=d_{\mathrm{et}}$. Since $(bc)d_{\mathrm{et}}=b d^a=d_{\mathrm{et}}$, uniqueness in Step 3 gives $bc=\mathrm{id}$. Since $(cb)d^a=c d_{\mathrm{et}}=d^a$, uniqueness in Step 6 gives $cb=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $b:F_{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega^{\mathrm{et}}_{U/V}$ is the required canonical isomorphism and identifies the derivations. These equations and the local arguments include empty schemes. No condition was imposed on the original morphism $f$.

source.place: Tag 04CS, final paragraph: corrected mutually-inverse pair c and c-double-prime and the two generator-normalized identities.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04CS, lemma-match-modules-differentials, all proof paragraphs. The final omitted verification is expanded using the elementary affine etale derivation calculation and existing Zariski-open determination. Tag 04BX, lemma-sheaf-differentials-etale-localization, supplies the only new prerequisite.

lean.note: The existing associated etale sheaf is kept literally as etaleTensorSectionsSheaf. An additive sheaf isomorphism with explicit sectionwise scalar compatibility is exactly a module-sheaf isomorphism, without constructing another associated module. The helper definitions are the sheafification and induced derivation explicitly specified by this item. No statement correction, finiteness hypothesis, coefficient lift or arbitrary comparison map.
